title: WW2 - OverSimplified (Part 2)
captions: manual (transcript is Albanian, likely auto-translated; analysis from text meaning only)
beats: Skillshare sponsor intro, then recap of Commonwealth joining the war
Winter War shows Soviet weakness; France's colonies split
Italy tries to take territory three times, with success shrinking each time
Tripartite Pact meant to deter the US; Roosevelt's campaign promise joke
U-boat problem and Britain's ideas, including the pykrete gag, ended by code breaking
Hitler pressures Balkans before Greece; Rommel pushes Britain back in Africa
Barbarossa: three million troops, big encirclement battles with numbers
Winter arrives; the frozen horse corpses gag shows poor planning
Japan's southern plan, Pearl Harbor, what Japan failed to hit
Japanese victories were based on speed not power, which will catch up with them
Stalingrad: Hitler shifts to oil, factories moved east, trapped army
Tide turns: Africa, Pacific, Italy invaded, Mussolini ousted
Americans and British argue; 'we'll do it your way' then 'we'll do it our way' repeated
D-Day: deception, weather delay, landing, then breakout
Berlin falls, Okinawa, atomic bombs, surrender
Occupation and aftermath; two superpowers lead into 'very cold' war pun

theory: This is a compression video: 6 years in 15 minutes, so the main move is sequencing with one foreshadowed cause per theatre, glued by a repeated gag. It teaches by narrative momentum rather than concept building, and caution applies because transcript is mistranslated.
velocity: Scene builder: a repeated visual gag can signal 'same structure as before'
Orchestrator: foreshadow the limit of a method before applying it
